### prerequisite_sentences
Four-point test, per edge:
1. P3←P2 "For a permitted job, the crew days booked are fixed only after the job's charges carry the permit administration fee." Connective "only after"; waited-on state is record-visible (an install_fee_assessed row of kind permit_admin_fee — "the job's charges"); no tool / id / snake_case; scope "for a permitted job" = condition. Single resolving write in this difficulty: only assess_permit_admin_fee_bf2a1df3 writes fee_kind permit_admin_fee. Derivation: reader of P3 sees the state → finds P2 whose rule prices "the permit administration fee of a permitted installation job" → writes it → inspection hold-back moves off the fall-through. One reading. PASS.
2. P3←P1 "A crew date for a job whose earlier crew date the customer moved or released is not booked until the job's charges carry the late reschedule fee owed for every such customer reschedule that was late or beyond the free count." Connective "not … until"; state record-visible (late_reschedule_fee rows); no tool/id; scope matches. Single resolving write: assess_reschedule_fee_4c3399da. P1 prices only "the most recent customer reschedule"; where more than one unbilled late reschedule exists the state could not be reached through P1 alone — checked per task. Also observation O-6: P1's share can be zero ("when Ridgeline has moved a crew date of the job two or more times the share charged is zero, so nothing is owed"), while the tool requires a positive amount; on such a world the waited-on state ("carry the late reschedule fee owed") has no write that brings it about. Checked per task.
3. P4←P3 "The trim capping charge is fixed only once the job record carries a booked crew date." Connective "only once"; state = install_jobs.scheduled_date / status scheduled; no tool. Within this difficulty only book_crew_date_2f98f590 sets a booked crew date on a job waiting to be scheduled (no task tool logs a reschedule or date change). PASS.
4. P6←P5 "On a job where Ridgeline itself moved or released a crew date with less than its notice, the failed-access fee is fixed only after the job carries the company reschedule credit owed for every such crew date." Connective "only after"; state = company_reschedule_credit rows; single resolving write issue_company_reschedule_credit_53c525ee. PASS.
5. P7←P6 "On a job that has had a failed-access visit, the lead-safe fee is not worked out until the job's charges carry the failed-access fee for every such visit." "not … until"; state = failed_access_fee rows; single write assess_failed_access_fee_5745b419. PASS.
6. P8←P7 "In a home built before the stated year, the interior casing charge is fixed only after the job's charges carry the lead-safe fee." "only after"; state = lead_safe_fee row; single write assess_lead_safe_fee_cf2f582a. PASS.
- No depended-on rule restates the blocked sentence (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P7 rules checked: none mentions crew-day booking, capping, the failed-access fee timing, the lead-safe timing or casing as something waiting on it).
- No other cross-problem ordering sentence in any extended rule. Two dating sentences carry an implicit dependency on a booked crew date that grounds no declared edge: P7 "dated the job's first crew day" and P8 "dated the crew day the casing is fitted" (and P6/P7 read `crew_days_planned`). On a world where the job already carries a booked crew date these are plain reads; on an unscheduled job they would be undeclared dependencies. Checked per task (O-7).
- Base rule sentences stating cross-problem order (install_scheduling "Homeowners-association … approval is obtained by the customer before a date is booked"; install_permits "A permitted job closes only after its final inspection has passed"; install_cancellation "only after its contract has been cancelled") ground no declared edge. HOA approval has no record field (customers / install_jobs schema), so it cannot be a record-visible state; observation O-8, checked against the persona per task.

Per component (task scope candidate): {P1..P4} carries multi-source factors (P2, P3, P4) and cross-difficulty factors; {P5..P8} carries multi-source (P5 rebook_wait_adder, P8 lead_safe_wall_prep) and cross-difficulty factors. Bounds 4–6 / ≥2 parameter / ≥1 method met by every policy.

Ladder structure:
- Every ladder has ≥3 pairwise-disjoint tiers including the fall-through; every tier is stated in the rule with its condition and value/method and is a branch of its `decides` binding; every `decides` names an input binding, never `result`; binding sets are disjoint within each policy.
- Each factor's fall-through equals the policy baseline for that input (P1 size 0 / whole base / share 1 / repeat 1 / release 1 → late reschedule fee; P2 → flat permit admin fee; P3 → units ÷ openings per crew day rounded up; P4 → rate × contract openings; P5 → method credit capped at charges owed; P6 → method failed-access fee; P7 → per-opening × openings floored at the minimum; P8 → rate × contract openings). Each `baseline.rule` sentence is in its `rule`, names the `baseline.params` keys, and yields a definite number with no factor applied. PASS.
- Labels: each `method` factor has at least one tier that changes the formula shape (P1 pro-rating by hours short; P2 per-opening 6.50 vs fee + 4 × excess vs flat; P3 split-day count vs weighted units vs plain; P4/P8 10-full-plus-discounted-tail vs uniform share; P5 started-week rate vs credit + 25 vs credit; P6 late fee × days vs failed + late vs failed; P7 floor × days vs +60 re-set vs plain floor). The remaining tiers of these ladders are share/number differences, which is acceptable inside a method ladder. All `parameter` factors substitute a number only. PASS.
- Distinct outcomes: no two tiers of any ladder name the same value symbolically. Two tier-param ladders select series/plan parameters whose numbers can coincide: contract_program_carryover / casing_program_carryover (military vs first-responder rate: equal for 1100, 2200, 4400 and 6600 series in window.yaml — 0.10/0.10, 0.10/0.10, 0.08/0.08, 0.06/0.06) and careline_parts_discount / careline_casing_discount (Premier 0.20 and Premier 3-Year 0.20 share a tier, so no clash; Basic 0.10, Plus 0.15, Estate 0.25 distinct). The coincidence is the window charter's own published rates, not a tier written twice; observation O-10, demonstrated per task only if the task's contract sits on such a series with such a program.
- Realism of conditions and outcomes (window/door replacement practice):
  - Reschedule fee scaled by job size, pro-rated by notice shortfall, waived by the company's own repeated moves, escalated for repeat late reschedules, raised when the slot is released or pushed far out — all are things an installer's scheduling policy weighs. Plausible.
  - Permit administration fee scaled by the energy-code window schedule length, contract valuation, safety-glazing schedule (tempered/laminated glazing in hazardous locations is checked by building departments under IRC R308), and a combined-filing share when a second released contract is filed together — plausible as the company's own administration schedule.
  - Crew pace lowered by build class (shapes, architectural wood) and frame material (wood-clad, fiberglass, composite), hold-back for a mid-job flashing inspection on permitted jobs, separate days for oversize units — real crew-planning considerations.
  - Capping/casing priced by priced openings with volume breaks, oversize weighting, color-matched coil or finish-matched stock, the contract's discount program, and a rush adder for short-lead coil — real trim-shop practice. The CareLine "parts discount" carried onto capping/casing (service.yaml defines `parts_discount_pct` as a discount "for parts used in a repair") is a member perk extended by the company's own rule; plausible as a published membership benefit, recorded as observation O-11, not a red.
  - Company reschedule credit by move length, notice, wait to the new date, factory delays, membership tier, and offset by the customer's own reschedules — goodwill-credit schedule; plausible.
  - Failed-access fee by crew days held (a lost multi-day block), repeat visits, the company's own credits, factory delays, membership courtesy, quick rebooking — plausible.
  - Lead-safe fee by containment days (RRP containment set per work day), shaped trim, oversize openings, re-staging after failed visits, rotted sills (more disturbed painted framing), bulk containment step-down — plausible.
  - No tier condition holds of every customer who reaches its write: e.g. P3 inspection fall-through ("no permit administration fee") holds exactly for non-permitted jobs; P8 prep fall-through for post-1978 homes; P5 notice tiers all lie under the 48-hour company notice, but the ladder splits that range (24/36) rather than restating it.
- No tier is read off a stamp field: every tier reads aggregates, dates, contract fields or variant names; the schema carries no field that names an outcome (no "late"/"failed_access" flag, no stored fee tier). Per-task check for seeded coincidences remains.

### findings
Charter-global, all observations (no charter-level red with a demonstrable consequence):
- O-1 (P2, P4, P8 vs install_agg_concurrent_jobs): per-opening amounts read the contract's openings, not the job's units; diverges only if the contract's openings differ from the job's `unit_count`. Bears on: task scopes containing P2/P4 (component 1) and P8 (component 2) — each task file checks the counts on its world.
- O-2 (P2 safety-glazing sentence): "the window contract" has no stated referent for a door job (compute reads the job's own window_contract_id → 0). Bears on any task whose P2 job is a door job.
- O-3 (P4, P8 service reads): first-active-holding semantics of CFIELD/CPARAM vs the rule's "active CareLine plan" when an active On-Call account coexists. Bears on tasks seeding two active service holdings.
- O-4 (P5 wait adder): rule silent when the job has no booked crew date now.
- O-5 (P6): a failed-access visit is identified only as customer + 0 notice.
- O-6 (P1 × P3 gate): a zero late reschedule fee (two or more company moves) cannot be written by a tool that takes a positive amount, so the P3 gate's state would be unreachable on such a world.
- O-7 (P6, P7, P8 dating/reads of crew_days_planned / first crew day): implicit dependency on a booked crew date that grounds no edge in component 2; harmless when the job is already scheduled.
- O-8 (base HOA sentence): HOA approval before booking has no record field; it rests on the persona.
- O-9 (install_site_charges S4 "charged per opening" not named in P4/P8 `superseded_clause`; replaced_by text covers the quantity).
- O-10 (program carryover tiers numerically equal on four window series).
- O-11 (CareLine repair-parts discount extended to new capping/casing).
- Contract-opening vs per-job reading, the P1 multi-reschedule reach and the P5 excess clause are carried into each task file as world checks.
